Output and Python API¶

Where files go¶

Output paths are relative to the process’s working directory. P.save_dir overrides P.supername; otherwise the default is im/<example>/<first-material-law>/. Choose a different directory for each run if you want to preserve results. Existing filenames may be overwritten.

Matplotlib uses the noninteractive Agg backend, so no plot window is expected. Open saved PNGs in an image viewer. Simulation output is ignored by Git.

Output flags¶

Set flags on P.O before initialisation. Missing flags default to false. The default adapter writes requested figures/arrays at each savetime and at the end. A custom callback replaces the corresponding default stage, so some examples intentionally produce different output.

Flag

Result under the output directory

plot_continuum

Continuum/*.png: velocity, density, pressure, shear rate, mean size.

plot_material_points

MP/*.png: material identity, speed, pressure.

plot_gsd_mp / plot_gsd_grid

GSD/*.png: grain fractions on particles or grid.

save_u

data/u_*.npy and data/v_*.npy, each (ny, nx).

save_density / save_s_bar

data/density_*.npy / data/s_bar_*.npy, each (ny, nx).

save_phi_MP

data/MP_phi_*.npy, columns x, y, phi_0, ..., phi_(ns-1).

measure_energy

Default callback records time, kinetic, potential, and the legacy strain- energy estimate in data/energy.npy; energy.png plots them.

measure_stiffness

Default end callback saves data/stiffness_material_*.npz.

With updated mechanics, O.save_diagnostics defaults to true and saves the separate verification ledger to data/diagnostics.json. See Updated mechanics, interpolation, transfers, and diagnostics for work budgets, sampling, and limitations.

The legacy strain-energy estimate is not a validated stored-energy or dissipation budget for every nonlinear material. Likewise, the saved grid density is a reconstruction from nodal mass, not the physical particle density evolved through F in updated mode.

Read a saved particle array with NumPy:

import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path

path = next(Path('im/my_sim/data').glob('MP_phi_*.npy'))
particles = np.load(path)
xy = particles[:, :2]
phi = particles[:, 2:]
print(xy.shape, phi.shape, phi.sum(axis=1))

The DP loading examples save data/pq_history.npz and pq_history.png. Here p is compression positive and q=sqrt(3 J2). Other saved pressure fields use the solver’s tension-positive convention. Bingham’s history pressure excludes the instantaneous bulk-viscous contribution to mean Cauchy stress.

Callbacks¶

All callbacks receive (L, P, G):

  • at_start: once before the run loop, including a bounded run.

  • after_every_timestep: after state and clock advancement.

  • after_every_savetime: when a step crosses the next requested save time.

  • at_end: once when the run ends, including a max_steps stop.

after_ever_timestep remains an alias for old inputs. Use the correctly spelled name in new code. A custom callback replaces that stage’s default adapter; it does not automatically add default plotting or energy recording. Explicitly call plotting.Plotting methods if both behaviours are needed.

For example, define this method on the input’s output class:

def after_every_savetime(self, L, P, G):
    from pathlib import Path
    import numpy as np
    from plotting import Plotting

    Plotting().draw_material_points(L, P, G)
    np.save(Path(P.save_dir)/f'stress_{P.tstep:06d}.npy',
            L.materials[0].stress)

Setting run(..., output=False) suppresses every callback. Large output frequencies can dominate runtime and disk usage; a small timestep does not imply that every step needs a plot.

Inspecting live state¶

L.materials contains one batch per material. Position and velocity arrays have shape (n, 3), stress and strain (n, 3, 3), and composition (n, ns). Geometry is two dimensional; the three-component/tensor representation is not a 3D solver. P.S holds material parameters, while L.materials holds evolving particle state.

Grid constitutive diagnostics such as G.pressure are mass-weighted sums. Use G.physical('pressure') to obtain the physical field. G.phi, G.s_bar, and G.shear_rate are already physical fields; do not divide them by mass again. Periodic endpoint columns duplicate one physical grid node.

run advances P.t and P.tstep. step intentionally does not. Neither saved NPY/NPZ output nor a bounded stop is a general checkpoint/restart facility; reconstructing all state and callback/controller history is not implemented.

2D material point method with grain-size segregation
